metaDescription: WordPress website for Telehealth.org, a telehealth education hub for clinicians: on-demand courses and webinars, news by topic, a newsletter and login.
summary: WordPress website for a telehealth education, news and training hub for clinicians.
overview: Telehealth.org describes itself as a trusted education hub for virtual care, offering courses, webinars, news and resources for healthcare professionals. Pixel2Tech built Telehealth.org's WordPress website as white-label development partner for a digital agency, on the Divi theme with WooCommerce for course sales.
challenge: The site serves two jobs at once: a news and resources publication that clinicians read regularly, and a training business that sells courses, bundles and credentials. Both had to sit under one navigation without the courses getting lost among articles.
approach: The main menu splits into News, Education, Newsletter and Resources, with a Log In button for learners. News is organized by topic, such as policy and compliance, clinical practice and technology, while Education groups on-demand courses, webinars, bundles and credential programs. A banner above the hero promotes the next webinar, and the home page leads to courses, the newsletter signup and the latest news.
outcome: A WordPress site that works as both a telehealth news source and a course catalog, with clear routes to courses, webinars and the newsletter on desktop and mobile. Readers who arrive for the news are always a click away from the course catalog.

process.title: Information architecture
process.body: Four menu groups separate news, education, the newsletter and resources such as research, the podcast and free downloads, so readers and learners each find their path.

process.title: Courses and checkout
process.body: On-demand courses, webinars, bundles and credential programs are sold through WooCommerce, with Edwiser Bridge connecting purchases to the learning platform.

process.title: News by topic
process.body: Articles are grouped into policy and compliance, clinical practice, technology and innovation, and business and market trends, with recent stories on the home page.

process.title: Webinars and newsletter
process.body: A banner above the hero promotes the next webinar, and newsletter signup calls to action appear in the hero and lower on the page.

whyItMatters: For an education brand, the news keeps clinicians coming back and the courses pay for it. A site that links the two well turns regular readers into learners.

faqs.q: What platform is the Telehealth.org website built on?
faqs.a: It runs on WordPress with the Divi theme, using WooCommerce for course sales and Edwiser Bridge to connect to the learning platform.
